The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start Docker Desktop or the Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` in PowerShell. Or use `docker-machine start default`. But the user might want to start Docker Desktop via command line. We can use `& "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"` or `Start-Process "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"`. Or use `docker start` to start a container. But they said "start Docker on window using docker start." That seems ambiguous. They might think docker start starts the Docker engine. But we can explain that docker start is for containers. To start Docker service, use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service`. Let's propose a command: `cmd /c "net start com.docker.service"`.

We can use the provided tool to execute a command. So we can call functions.cmd_controller_execute with command: `net start com.docker.service`. But we need to ensure it's correct. The tool expects a string of Windows command line instructions. So we can pass `net start com.docker.service`. That will start the Docker service. Alternatively, if Docker Desktop is installed, we can start it via `Start-Process "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"`. But the simplest is `net start com.docker.service`.
